light: This is one ordinary frame pulled from a normal handheld video shot by a friend with a consumer camera at eye level, simply recording what happens, not composing a photo. The framing is casual and a little off: something is cut by the edge of the frame. Almost everything in the frame is in focus, nothing blurred out: the cluttered background stays fully readable. The only light is what the place really has, and each person and object gets light according to where it stands; correctly exposed, the side near the opening a little brighter and cooler, the far corners dimmer. Colours of an ordinary video with automatic white balance and almost no correction: moderate contrast, soft highlights, mild sensor noise and light compression, faint motion blur on anything moving. Skin with pores, small blemishes and uneven tone; hair with stray strands; clothes with real creases, dust and wear. People are caught mid-action, unposed.
look: Ordinary handheld home video filmed by a friend with a consumer camera at eye level, small natural shakes and casual slightly imperfect framing, everything in the room in focus, only the light the place really has, correctly exposed, automatic white balance, mild sensor noise; real skin and natural hands; people move naturally and unposed, nothing staged; no music.

anchors.prompt: Place this same man in a new place. The place is a real, messy home garage-workshop of a working-class house in Latin America: concrete floor with old stains and cement dust, a wooden workbench covered in tools, tins, rags and offcuts, a pegboard with hanging tools, stacked plastic buckets, a bicycle leaning on the wall, bare painted brick walls with damp patches, the wide garage door on the left open to the street. He is the man of the reference photo — same face, same dark curly hair, same short salt-and-pepper beard — wearing a faded olive-green work shirt with the sleeves rolled up to the elbows, stained with paint and dust, and a worn brown leather apron over it. He is crouching on the concrete floor beside the two halves of an old white porcelain toilet sawn in half lengthwise: the flat cut face shows the inside of the curved trap channel lined with a thick, rough, layered crust of yellow-brown and grey limescale, like stone, narrowing the passage to less than half, lying on a folded dirty blanket. An angle grinder lies on the floor beside them with its cable across the frame. A dust mask hangs around his neck, clear safety glasses pushed up on his forehead, white dust on his shoulders and in his hair. He looks up at the camera, mouth caught mid-word. Medium shot from about one and a half metres, the camera at the height of a crouching person. Light: flat overcast daylight coming in through the open garage door on the left, plus one plain fluorescent tube on the ceiling; the side near the door a little brighter and cooler, the back corners dimmer.

Same place, same framing and same light, a few seconds later: he holds one half of the toilet tilted toward the camera with one hand, pointing at the crust with the other, looking at the camera. He keeps exactly the same clothes: the faded olive-green work shirt with rolled sleeves and the worn brown leather apron.

Same place and same light as the first image, but a different camera angle: The camera now looks toward the open garage door: the neighbour, the neighbour of the second input image (his face): a heavy-set man around 65, bald on top with grey hair on the sides, a thick grey moustache, a faded light-blue checked short-sleeve shirt with a pen in the breast pocket, reading glasses hanging on a cord around his neck, stands in the doorway with a folded newspaper in one hand, staring down at the cut toilet halves on the floor with a frown of disbelief; the presenter is crouched at the right edge of the frame, seen from the side, looking up at him.

Same place, same framing and same light, a few seconds later: the neighbour has put his hands on his hips, shaking his head slightly; the presenter at the right edge looks up at him. The neighbour is exactly the man of the second input image (his face).

Same place and same light as the first image, but a different camera angle: The camera is back on the presenter: he crouches beside the cut toilet halves on the blanket, turned toward the garage door on the left (the neighbour is out of the frame), with a half grin, one hand resting on top of a toilet half. He keeps exactly the same clothes: the faded olive-green work shirt with rolled sleeves and the worn brown leather apron.

Same place, same framing and same light, a few seconds later: he looks back at the camera, one hand flat on top of the cut toilet half, eyebrows raised. He keeps exactly the same clothes: the faded olive-green work shirt with rolled sleeves and the worn brown leather apron.

Same place, same framing and same light, a few seconds later: still crouched, he holds up his index finger toward the camera, a determined look. He keeps exactly the same clothes: the faded olive-green work shirt with rolled sleeves and the worn brown leather apron.

clips.text: Esto es lo que tienes adentro de tu inodoro. Y no, no se va limpiando.
clips.action: He points with a dusty finger at the yellow-brown crust inside the cut trap, then looks back at the camera and talks.
The neighbour in the doorway frowns, points down at the cut toilet with his newspaper and speaks to the presenter in disbelief; the presenter only listens, looking up at him.
clips.who: the neighbour (the fourth reference image is his face)
clips.voice: the neighbour (the fourth reference image is his face), in Spanish with a neutral Latin American accent, the gruff, amused voice of a 65-year-old man; the presenter does NOT speak

clips.text: Uno viejo, tranquilo. Mira por qué lo saqué.
clips.action: He answers toward the neighbour off-frame on the left with a half grin and taps the cut toilet with his hand.

clips.text: La buena noticia: esto se saca sin cambiar el inodoro. Con vinagre caliente, una piedra pómez y un alambre. Y te lo muestro completo ahora mismo, no al final.
clips.action: He talks to the camera with conviction, brushing white dust off his hands, counting on his fingers.
